primitives.name: Binary Reverse Engineering
primitives.verbatim_quote: # RE repo vetting — odds/signal ingestion (9 repos + 2 curated files) Metadata: api.github.com only; nothing cloned.
primitives.assumptions: The system operates under the assumption that binary-level analysis does not yield actionable HTTP endpoint data.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When applied to networked systems, binary RE fails to produce interpretable JSON structures required for odds ingestion.

layer2.mapping: Binary RE maps to a kernel of static analysis that lacks dynamic HTTP context necessary for odds pipeline integration.
layer2.telemetry: Star count discrepancy between curated metadata and live GitHub API indicates misalignment with current development velocity.

primitives.name: HAR to OpenAPI Derivation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Turns mitmproxy captures into OpenAPI 3 specs that generate typed HTTP clients — the "record XHR → derive a client" technique already used for ESPN `site.web.api` odds and Kalshi public markets.
primitives.assumptions: HTTP traffic captured via HAR can be reliably parsed into structured API specifications without loss of semantic fidelity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when HAR captures include authenticated sessions violating terms of service or lack sufficient metadata for spec generation.

layer2.mapping: HAR captures are transformed into executable API clients through formal specification derivation, enabling automated odds ingestion.
layer2.telemetry: Verification of derived OpenAPI specs against known public endpoints ensures correctness of client generation.

primitives.name: Offline Binary Forensics
primitives.verbatim_quote: Hex editor + pattern language for binary/disk forensics; reads bytes off a disk or memory dump, not HTTP responses.
primitives.assumptions: Offline forensic tools operate exclusively on byte streams and do not interface with network protocols.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When attempting to extract HTTP data from binaries, offline forensics fail due to absence of network-layer abstraction.

layer2.mapping: Offline binary forensics align with low-level data recovery but diverge from high-level HTTP protocol consumption needed for odds pipelines.
layer2.telemetry: Absence of network stack in forensic tools precludes use in real-time odds acquisition workflows.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core tension lies in distinguishing between binary-level reverse engineering and HTTP-based signal extraction. The former, exemplified by morluto/rea and WerWolv/ImHex, focuses on static analysis of compiled artifacts, which inherently lacks the dynamic semantics required for odds ingestion. Conversely, HAR-to-OpenAPI derivation bridges this gap by converting captured HTTP exchanges into structured API contracts. This transformation enables GSI to perform Bayesian inference on endpoint validity while GSE executes state transitions from raw capture to typed client. The failure mode arises when repositories claim relevance but do not support the necessary protocol abstraction—e.g., fitness-tracking SDKs or phishing tools—which violate both technical and ethical constraints of the odds pipeline.
